parts.text: This design was built against the tetel repository at commit 57bd0e29a6c8bd3861f3982bebe3486f80e0453d with a clean working tree
every code citation below refers to that state.
NONE
TET-28's "workspace-rooted" requirement is NOT decidable from today's capture in the case that matters most.
When look_grep finds matches
it records one extent entry per matched file
keyed on that file's resolved path
with label "<file> (grep
and the search root appears nowhere in what is captured
the code's own comment says the entries are keyed "not by the search root or the grep command line".
A repo-wide grep and a single-file grep that matched the same file therefore capture byte-identical extents.
Every genuine census of a symbol an implementer is told to modify falls in this positive-match case
because the symbol's definition site matches.
NONE
The zero-match case IS decidable today
and it shows the shape the fix should take
a no-match grep records one entry whose key is the resolved search root and whose Marker { root
state } is resolved from that same root
so "was this bounded negative repo-wide" reduces to comparing two tool-captured strings on one entry
key versus world_root.
TET-5's per-observation markers and the unconditional -H made this comparison meaningful
they did not extend it to the positive-match case.
NONE
The census therefore needs a small capture extension before any refusal can exist
look_grep should record
for every search
one root-level search entry
key = the resolved search root
a label carrying the pattern and the match-file count
marker resolved from the search root
alongside the existing per-file match entries
making the match and no-match cases uniform.
"Workspace-rooted" then has one decidable definition covering both cases
the search entry's key equals its own world_root
a byte comparison of two strings the same look_grep call captured from the same canonicalized directory.
No author-typed input participates on either side.
NONE
A census check cannot be built on labels
and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema.
At mint time only key
world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry
the observation's kind is dropped
and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label
where an author-chosen pattern containing " in " or "(grep:
" would make parsing ambiguous.
The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry
the observation kind and the search pattern
following the exact precedent world_root set
#[serde(default)]
with the empty value read as "predates the field
not eligible" rather than guessed about.
Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement
whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture.
The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries
so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains
and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand
both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.
NONE
A mention-triggered refusal (candidate 2) is off-charter and already measured dead in this repository.
The charter forbids heuristic refusals outright
and scope.rs records the measurement
string-matching symbol references was tried for the note-outside-extent check and rejected because it "would have flagged a legitimate quotation ... while missing both real overreaches"
naming a symbol is normal
concluding about it is the failure
"and those two are not distinguishable by string matching".
A refusal wired to that detector would refuse honest memos
which is precisely what scope.rs's "refusing would make the honest case unwritable" disposition exists to prevent.
This also means the README Direction entry for this feature
"requiring a workspace-rooted search behind a claim that names a symbol"
is phrased as the mention-triggered shape and should be corrected to the declared-target shape when this ships.
NONE
The decidable trigger is declaration (candidate 1)
a modification target is a structured record the author creates
a symbol string plus a fact citation
and the refusal fires only on a declared target whose cited fact carries no qualifying census entry.
This sits inside the machine partition's own stated principle
that machine failures are "objective contradictions between a document and the record it claims to rest on
decidable without a human"
a target row is exactly a pointer at evidence
and "you did not point at your evidence" is the README's own example of a decidable question.
The refusal's remedy is singular
run the workspace-rooted grep for that symbol
mint the fact
cite it (or withdraw the target)
so refusal rather than report is the right disposition for the declared-but-uncensused case
by the same discriminator under which scope.rs chose report
only a person can tell context from conclusion
nothing is left to tell.
NONE
Under-declaration
the memo recommends modifying a symbol it never declared
cannot be a refusal and must not be silently absorbed either.
Deciding from prose that a sentence "tells an implementer to modify X" is a heuristic read of English
exactly the class the charter routes to the human-owed partition or nowhere
scope.rs's measured precedent shows the symbol-detector that trigger would need flags quotation and misses conclusion.
The design therefore makes the omission visible instead of detected:
(a) once a workspace declares any target
render emits a Modification targets section
and once any claim exists it emits the section even when empty
"Modification targets
none declared"
so a memo that recommends changes while declaring nothing shows a hole where the census should be
in front of every reader
and (b) check's standing non-coverage list
whose first entry is already "dependents that never declared themselves"
gains a census-specific line ("a recommendation whose target was never declared") so the blind spot is printed rather than implicit.
NONE
Where the refusal lives
at declaration
then re-verified at check.
The `target` verb refuses to create a target whose cited fact carries no qualifying census entry
the same authoring-time shape as fact refusing on an empty pending buffer ("a fact needs a preceding look/run"
a target needs a preceding rooted census).
Because a fact's extent is immutable once minted and a target is immutable once declared
this makes "every declared target is censused" a workspace invariant
and no render-path refusal is needed for workspace-authored documents

render's job is only to emit the targets section. check independently re-verifies the rendered document against its snapshot and reports [uncensused-target] as a machine failure in the partition's scope line
which is what catches a hand-authored or tampered document that never passed through the refusing verb.
Like notes_outside_extent and mint_windows
that check runs only when a snapshot ships
target rows are reported human-owed as unverifiable
consistent with the standing choice that a missing snapshot is human-owed rather than a machine failure.
The verb must be one dispatch shared by CLI and MCP
the pattern look and fact already use
because this codebase has recorded a CLI/MCP drift on exactly such a duplicated act.
NONE
The rooting predicate
census entry's key byte-equals its own world_root
is satisfiable and fails closed.
On this machine and repo the two spellings (fs-canonicalized search root
git rev-parse --show-toplevel) agree byte-for-byte
so an honestly rooted grep satisfies the predicate
and if the two tools ever disagree on spelling
the mismatch refuses an honest census loudly rather than accepting an unrooted one silently
because inequality can only ever deny rooting
never grant it.
Two hardenings belong in the implementation
look_grep should itself compare the canonicalized search root against the marker's root at capture time and store the search entry's key in the marker's spelling when they name the same directory
so check stays a pure byte comparison
and the agreement should be pinned by a test
since one probe on one machine shows the common case
not an invariant.
NONE
The qualifying-census predicate
a declared target (symbol S
citing fact F) is censused iff F's captured extent contains a search entry whose kind field says it is a whole-search record
whose pattern field byte-equals S
whose key byte-equals its own world_root
and whose world_root is git-backed (neither the no-git sentinel nor the empty predates-the-field value).
Byte-equality of pattern to symbol is the only sound decidable comparison available
grep is invoked with the pattern verbatim (-e <pattern>)
so a looser rule like "pattern contains the symbol" would accept a grep whose pattern merely embeds S in a longer string and therefore matches a strict subset of S's textual occurrences
while anything semantically wider would require deciding containment between regular expressions.
Symbols that are not literal strings in the system grep's dialect are a stated limit of the census
not a case the check adjudicates.
NONE
The census's blind spots are boundable from what the capture actually does
and belong in check's printed non-coverage:
(a) a textual grep cannot see dynamic dispatch
re-exports and aliased imports
or macro-generated and string-assembled identifiers;
(b) the traversal is the system grep's
tetel deliberately shells out to it rather than reimplementing a dialect
so platform rules about symlinked directories and the -I binary skip bound what a "repo-wide" search physically visited;
(c) rooting says where the search started
not which tree it should have been
whether the censused root is the tree the memo designs against stays with the reader
alongside the existing per-root tree-state report;
(d) whether anyone read the census is the insincere-examination ceiling
capture makes the extent honest
not the interpretation
and (e) under-declared targets
by construction.
The report mechanism for printing exactly this kind of standing limit already exists as the NON_COVERAGE list.
NONE
The feature's implementation surface is small and depends on nothing beyond what this memo's facts describe
one additional recorded entry in look_grep
two serde-defaulted structured fields on the extent entry (following world_root's own compatibility precedent)
one new append-only record type whose authoring verb refuses uncensused declarations from one dispatch shared by CLI and MCP
one rendered section beside the existing ledger and Facts tables
and one machine check with its human-owed and non-coverage lines.
In particular it requires no TET-27 mechanism
no code-to-graph links
no commit references
no dependency propagation
so shipping it first imposes no design debt on that exploration.
NONE
The ticket's trigger as written is undecidable in tetel's own record model
verified against the record types
a claim is only { id
cited fact ids
a prose block only { heading
cited claim ids }
and nothing on either surface types a record as a recommendation or an instruction
prose creation is deliberately ungated because "prose is where the author talks
not where they're audited".
So "a memo whose recommendation names a target" denotes no set of records any check can enumerate
any implementation of it would have to read English.
The claim verb also supplies the refusal precedent the target verb extends
claim already refuses without --cites and on unknown fact ids
so "a structured record must cite a real record of the right shape" is the house's established authoring-refusal pattern.
NONE
This design was built against the tetel repository at commit 67191f58c925fcaaed5f9b2ebe218bb23fcded8e ("tet28
pin the census refusal
and make the parity guard real")
with a clean working tree at the start of authoring
the TET-28 modification-target implementation is present in the tree this design reads
and the memo plus its snapshot are the one addition this workspace makes.
NONE
TET-29's trigger must be a declaration
not a detection
by the same argument TET-28 implemented rather than merely designed.
"Any design or fix that transplants a mechanism from another site" denotes no enumerable set of records
nothing in the record model types a claim or prose block as a transplant
and deciding from English (or from comparing code across two sites) that a fix "transplants" is a heuristic read
the class scope.rs measured dead for symbol mentions ("naming a symbol the code you read calls is normal
concluding about it is the failure
the two are not distinguishable by string matching") and the class targets.rs's shipped doc comment rules out as a refusal trigger.
So a transplant is a record the author declares
the refusal attaches to the declaration
and under-declaration is handled the way TET-28 handles it
an always-rendered section that shows its hole
plus a printed non-coverage line
never a detector.
NONE
"Transcribed verbatim" cannot be an honour-system field
and does not need to be
the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output.
Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls
a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path
grep match lines
a process's merged stream)
no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand
and output is immutable after mint
so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check.
Typing is the selection mechanism
not the trust
the author types the premise
but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb.
This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection ("refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact
the author cannot type an extent
and here could not invent support
only select it")
and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.
NONE
The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path
and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel.
A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`
indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture
because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim
the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section
which the "never paraphrase" constraint endorses rather than tolerates.
Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax
which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's "language-agnostic by construction" doctrine excludes.
Two capture modes genuinely fight containment
grep-derived match outputs interleave "lineno:" prefixes between lines
and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output
so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file
that is guidance about which observation to select from
not a new rule
since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes.
Weaker relations fail
per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote
and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain
both are paraphrase with extra steps.
NONE
Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness
and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made.
Fact.output is built at mint by joining the buffer entries' non-empty outputs with "\n"
and the per-entry boundaries are not stored
so "substring of fact.output" can be satisfied by text straddling the seam between two observations
bytes that were never contiguous in anything the author actually saw
e.g. the tail of one file's capture concatenated with the head of another's.
The fix is a serde-defaulted per-entry field on ExtentEntry recording the entry's output byte length
mirroring exactly how kind and pattern were added for TET-28
boundaries become reconstructible from lengths (skipping zero-length entries
matching the mint-time filter)
the premise relation is then "verbatim substring of a single observation's output"
and a donor fact minted before the field existed is ineligible with the same remedy TET-28 gives legacy facts
re-look and re-mint.
Absent means not recorded
never guessed.
NONE
The transplant record's shape follows from precedents already shipped
one field at a time.
A transplant is an append-only record declared by a new verb (one dispatch shared by CLI and MCP
one new Kind variant and counter):
(a) the donor is a citation of exactly ONE fact
the same single-citation rationale targets.rs states ("a target resting on 'one of these several facts' would leave which one undecided")
and a fact citation rather than a typed path because the donor site is then the fact's captured extent
which no author can type;
(b) premise rows are verbatim selections from that donor fact's output (per C3-C5)
immutable once selected
a selection of immutable bytes has nothing to revise honestly
and withdrawable with --why
mirroring target's withdraw-not-revise discipline;
(c) a premise is discharged by citing a claim
in a separate later act
and because `tetel claim` refuses without --cites and on unknown fact ids
a discharge claim rests on at least one real fact by construction
the ticket's "must that claim itself rest on a fact?" is answered yes with zero new machinery;
(d) a discharge can be superseded by a later discharge citing a different claim
so a refuted-and-replaced claim does not strand its premise.
NONE
The transplant's destination should be a citation of a live modification target (T#)
not a typed path and not an independent record
the two features compose.
A transplant installs the donor's mechanism at a site the design necessarily tells the implementer to modify
so under TET-28's own rule that site should already be a declared target
making the transplant verb refuse a destination that is not a live target turns one declaration into a forcing function for the other
and narrows TET-28's admitted under-declaration blind spot for exactly the fix-shape that produced the motivating defect.
The composition costs nothing at the edge cases
a green-field destination (new code
new symbol) is still censusable
because censuses() deliberately accepts a NoMatch search
"a symbol with no occurrences is censused by the grep that established it has none"
so declaring a target for a symbol that does not exist yet works today
and the destination-holds claims get a named
censused destination instead of a prose phrase.
What the tool cannot verify
that the cited target really is where the mechanism lands
and stays printed as non-coverage rather than guessed at.
NONE
An undischarged premise must be a legal workspace state
so the ticket's refusal cannot all move to the verb the way TET-28's did.
The instrument works by transcribe-first
the author selects the donor's premises before knowing whether each holds at the destination
the confrontation the section exists to force.
Refusing a premise row that cites no claim at declaration time would demand the destination-holds claim exist before the premise can be recorded
inverting that order (answer first
transcribe after) and pushing an author who cannot yet discharge a premise toward not declaring it at all
the same "refusing would make the honest case unwritable to catch the dishonest one" failure scope.rs's discriminator names.
TET-28 never faced this because a census either exists or does not
a premise inventory is built across time.
So the workspace invariant enforced at the verb is only "every premise is a genuine quotation of the cited donor's capture" (plus
donor fact exists and carries span boundaries
destination target exists and is live
a discharge cites an existing live claim);
"every premise is discharged" is not a workspace invariant at all
it is a property of the finished document.
NONE
The refusals land on three surfaces
each the earliest that can decide its own question.
(1) At the verb
quotation invariants
donor fact exists and is span-eligible
premise text is a verbatim substring of a single observation's output
destination is a live target
a discharge names an existing live claim.
These are per-record and decidable at creation
exactly like target's census refusal.
(2) At `render --out`
a live transplant with an undischarged premise (none cited
or its discharge claim withdrawn) refuses the write.
This is deliberately later than the verb (the intermediate state is legal while authoring) and deliberately earlier than check (the ticket's placement)
--out is the act that writes the reviewable artifact and its snapshot under the pinned policy that a rendered memo is never hand-edited
so a memo with a declared-but-unexamined premise should fail to come into existence rather than exist and fail
the remedy is singular
discharge the premise
or withdraw it or its transplant with --why.
A preview render (no --out) still assembles
marking undischarged rows loudly
so mid-work visibility is preserved
this render/--out asymmetry is new
and it is the design's most debatable departure.
re-verification of everything above against the shipped snapshot
both directions
since tampering can go either way (a transplant row the snapshot lacks
a snapshot premise whose text is not contained in its donor fact's output
a premise whose discharge claim is withdrawn or missing)
as a machine failure in the same partition as uncensused targets
with rows in a snapshotless document reported human-owed as unverifiable
the standing choice for snapshot-dependent findings.
Containment is re-checked byte-for-byte from facts.jsonl
which already ships full outputs
check runs nothing and fetches nothing to do it.
NONE
The containment relation was tested against the motivating case itself
at the source
and it passes
with one correction to the ticket's framing.
The missed premise ("its parent is remote-known or was walked earlier in this same session"
remote_utils.rs:4576 in lonic-forklift at HEAD) is contiguous bytes in a raw capture of the donor file
both as a single clause within one line and as the full seven-line `//` comment with its prefixes
so the verbatim-substring refusal admits it without any comment-syntax knowledge.
But the premise does NOT live in the donor function's `///` doc block
collect_changed_closure's doc block never states the insert-before-check discipline or its ordering premise
both live only in the body comment below the signature.
So the ticket's phrase "the donor's comment-stated premises" must not be operationalised as "the donor's doc block"
the relation has to range over whatever bytes the author captured of the donor site
and a premise stated at a call site or in a body comment is selectable exactly when the author's donor fact folded an observation that covers it
the relation thereby pressures the author to capture the donor widely enough
and a known-but-uncaptured premise demands another look
not a typed row.
today's repaired destination twin states the once-missed condition as one gradeable sentence ("Sound only parents-first
a child that marked a parent-explained hash would otherwise short-circuit the explaining parent's own audit")
which is concrete evidence that the discharge obligation this design demands
one claim per premise
stating that it holds at the destination
fits in a single claim proposition for the hardest observed case.
NONE
The rendered section follows compose.rs's shipped conventions with one deliberate difference.
A "## Transplants" section renders beside the modification-target section
per live transplant
the donor fact id with its extent labels (labels
never absolute keys
the committed-document rule)
the destination target id and symbol
and one entry per live premise carrying the selected text verbatim in a fenced block with the discharging claim id beside it
withdrawn transplants and premises are dropped
and once any claim exists the section renders even when empty ("none declared")
because the hole is the finding
the same visibility answer to under-declaration the target section shipped.
The deliberate difference
compose.rs refuses to inline captured output into the document because output is unbounded
but a premise is an author-bounded selection
not a whole capture
so inlining it verbatim is both safe and the entire point
the reader must see the donor's clause on the page
spelled the way the donor's file spells it
or the section is a list of opaque pointers.
Fenced blocks rather than table cells because a premise legitimately spans lines and markdown table cells cannot carry multi-line verbatim text without escaping
which would violate byte-fidelity.
NONE
What the mechanism cannot catch is boundable and belongs in check's printed NON_COVERAGE list
which exists for exactly this ("a refusal that fired is easily read as coverage it never claimed").
(a) a transplant the author never declared
no refusal can reach it
the empty section is its only trace;
(b) premises the donor never wrote down
the relation selects from captured text
so a premise that lives in the donor's structure rather than its comments has nothing to select;
(c) premises outside the captured extent
a donor fact that folded too narrow a look cannot yield a premise from the lines it never captured;
(d) shallow selection
the tool verifies that selected bytes are the donor's
never that they are all the load-bearing ones
selecting one convenient clause and stopping is invisible to any format-level check
because deciding what counts as a premise is design judgment (the ticket says so) and deciding a selection is too small is a truth-check
the insincere-examination ceiling this project registered as permanently out of reach;
(e) whether the discharge claim actually addresses its premise
and whether the cited target really is the mechanism's destination
the claim is graded by a grounding pass as written
and the linkage is graded by nobody;
(f) a donor comment that is itself wrong
verbatim quotation establishes provenance
None of these is reachable by a format-level refusal
so printing them is the honest disposition
not a fallback.
NONE
The mechanism's value is precisely that it moves one property across check's oldest declared blind spot
and grounding then does the rest.
Per the ticket's account of the FORK-94 trail
recorded here as the ticket's report
not re-established
the defective remedy was graded supports twice
because the violated property was asserted by no claim at all
that situation is exactly the first entry in check's standing non-coverage list
"dependents that never declared themselves"
and a grounder that grades propositions as written has nothing to grade where there is no proposition.
Every piece of this design funnels toward converting that absent proposition into a present one
the premise row forces the donor's condition onto the page as captured bytes
and the discharge obligation forces a claim that the condition holds at the destination
a claim like any other
resting on facts by construction
entering the evidence ledger
graded by the next grounding pass
revisable and then out-of-proof until regraded.
The tool never judges whether the claim is true
it refuses only the shape in which the question goes unasked.
And the hardest observed case shows the converted claim fits in one sentence
today's repaired destination states the once-missed condition in a single doc-comment sentence
first-hand evidence that the discharge obligation is one gradeable proposition
not an essay.
NONE
The implementation surface is small and every piece extends a mechanism already in the tree
one serde-defaulted per-entry output-length field on ExtentEntry (the same compatibility precedent that added kind and pattern
with the same absent-means-ineligible reading)
one new record kind with its counter and id prefix
one transplants.jsonl appended by one CLI/MCP-shared dispatch
shipped by adding one line to snapshot.rs's deliberately-enumerated SNAPSHOT_FILES (whose targets.jsonl entry already documents why a record log must ship
without it the refusal "would hold only inside the workspace that authored the memo")
one rendered section beside render_targets
one completeness refusal in the render --out path
one check re-verifying from files the snapshot already carries (transplant machine findings beside uncensused_targets
unverifiable rows human-owed without a snapshot)
and the new NON_COVERAGE lines.
Nothing parses any programming language
nothing is re-run at check time
and no aggregate
or document-level verdict is introduced anywhere.
NONE
This design was taken against tetel at commit e19a4694bedd1bd2bda91626362f9c2d05f35274
every claim below describes that tree.
NONE
Every input the ticket names is present and travels with the memo
prose.jsonl and claims.jsonl ship inside `<memo>.tetel/`
each event in them carries a `timestamp
the prose→claim citation edges are the `cite` field of prose events
and a rendered ledger claim id is byte-identical to the workspace claim id.
Two things the ticket does not name are also true and constrain the design
both loaders discard every timestamp
so the check must read the logs rather than the loaded types
and a prose block's own id is never written into the rendered document
so a residue line naming `P4` names something no reader of the memo alone can locate.
NONE
The ticket's anchor
"revised since the last grounding pass"
would have gone silent on the finding the ticket cites.
`brief::build` returns every ledger claim unconditionally
including already-grounded ones ("A claim leaves this list only by leaving the ledger itself
never by having been reported on")
so every subsequent pass re-grades a claim whose wording never changed and appends records with strictly later timestamps against the same digest.
This is measured
in the two shipped memos
tet28's C9 carries ten records on one unchanged digest from three passes spanning 1690 seconds
and tet28's C13 was graded `qualifies` by two passes 918 seconds apart on unchanged text.
So an anchor at the *latest* grading advances past any fix-round prose edit as soon as one more pass runs
and the FORK-94 trail the ticket describes ran six rounds.
The anchor must instead be the *earliest* record grading the claim's current wording
the moment that wording first entered proof
which a later pass over unchanged text cannot move.
NONE
The residue rule is
a prose block is listed iff (a) it is not a heading and carries at least one citation
(b) every id it cites resolves to a claim in the memo's ledger
(c) every one of those claims is in proof under the predicate `analyze_ledger` already uses
some evidence record whose `proposition_digest` matches sha256 of the claim's current proposition
with the empty digest grandfathered
and (d) the timestamp of the event that set the block's current text is strictly greater than the maximum
over its cited claims
of that claim's earliest in-proof record timestamp.
Clause (d) settles the ticket's two ambiguities together
the per-claim anchor is the earliest record grading the current wording
and the per-block anchor is the latest of those
so a block is listed only once its whole evidence base has settled and its text has moved since.
Run against the two shipped memos it lists nothing
tet28's and tet29's post-grounding prose revisions each accompanied a claim revision
so the new wording's first proof postdates the edit
and tet28's six post-grounding revisions that did not are heading blocks.
Given a FORK-94-shaped edit
tet29's P11 moved 600 seconds past the last first proof with no claim touched
it lists exactly that block and nothing else
and giving one of its cited claims a later first proof clears it.
NONE
The residue is about any prose whose text postdates the settling of what it cites
not about revision specifically
the block's timestamp is the one that set its current text
whether that was its `Create` or its last `Revise`
both of which carry a `timestamp` on the prose event.
Including creations closes an identical exposure at near-zero cost in listings.
It is identical because a paragraph written fresh under already-graded claims rests on them exactly as ungradedly as a rewritten one.
It is near-zero cost because a paragraph created in a fix round to carry a new assertion normally cites a new claim
and a new claim is not in proof when the paragraph is written
by the time any pass has put it in proof
that first proof postdates the paragraph
so the block never becomes listable.
What creation-counting does catch is the case worth catching
a new paragraph written under nothing but old
already-settled claims.
NONE
The first-proof anchor makes the line unclearable by anything that did not look at the prose
and that is deliberate
a further grounding pass over unchanged wording appends records with later timestamps but cannot move the earliest one
so re-grounding never blesses a listed block.
The only two things that clear it are reverting the text
and revising or adding a cited claim and having the new wording graded
which is exactly the remedy the finding calls for
since the defect is prose asserting something no claim carries.
stated rather than hidden
a listing has no cheap discharge
so a flow-only edit made after a memo's claims have settled stays listed until the memo's next claim revision
and a memo shipped with such an edit ships the line.
This is a smaller version of a cost this project has already paid badly once
`no scope declared` printed one undischargeable line per claim and buried the findings that were about the document under a constant
but it differs where it matters
this line is about *this* document
never fires on all blocks at once
and names two concrete acts that clear it.
NONE
This is the first check to compare timestamps across processes

rather than by comparing timestamps
keeps the whole acknowledgement mechanism free of clock comparisons.
